newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks end up, shrugging off Dow slide.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks end up, shrugging off Dow slide.

text.p: An increasingly buoyant Australian share market shrugged off the Dow's dive to end slightly firmer on Thursday, encouraged by Coca-Cola Amatil's tie-up with the Philippine's San Miguel and a local bank merger.
Brokers said many investors hugging the sidelines in recent days seemed to shed their fears about the Dow and jump back into the fray in afternoon trade, boosting volumes and prices.

"People said this correction in the United States has been very well telegraphed, we've seen enough selling for now and maybe it's now time to knuckle down and start looking for a bit of value," BNP Equities broker John Bowie Wilson said.

The All Ordinaries Index closed up 5.8 points at 2,361, bouncing back from its morning low of 2,341 as the focus swung from Wall Street's paranoia about rising U.S. interest rates to local corporate activity.

C-C Amatil announced it would merge with San Miquel Corp's Coca Cola bottling operations, a move that will see C-C Amatil issue A$3.4 billion worth of shares and San Miguel take a 25 percent stake in CC Amatil.
Analysts welcomed the move as very earnings per share positive, rocketing C-C Amatil's share price up 95 cents to an intra-day high of A$12.90, its highest level since February 19.
C-C Amatil closed up 85 cents at A$12.80 on hefty volumes of 1.1 million shares traded, helping bolster overall market trade to A$800.1 million, its highest this week.
The other major focus was Bank of Melbourne's announcement that it had agreed to a Westpac Banking Corp A$1.435 billion takeover bid pitched at A$9.75 per share.
The reaction was mixed, with Bank of Melbourne ending up 70 cents at A$9.50 having earlier raced to the bid price of A$9.75.
Westpac closed unchanged at A$6.88, after dipping to A$6.75. Broker and analysts' views were mixed on whether the bid would be enough to deter rivals like National Australia Bank LtD.
However most believed the bid would be able to jump the regulatory hurdles put in its path by the anti-monopoly body, Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC).
Treasurer Peter Costello must also approve the merger.
Other regional banks rode Bank of Melbourne's coat-tails higher on speculation about further regional bank takeovers.
Adelaide Bank Ltd closed up 11 cents at A$4.36, while Bendigo Bank Ltd closed up 16 cents at A$4.91.
Elsewhere, Goodman Fielder Ltdclosed up one cent at A$1.64 on volume of 10.76 billion, which brokers described as non-descript institutional shuffling.

Santos Ltd topped the volume list early on with 7.1 million shares traded, down 29 cents at A$4.71 as it went ex-dividend and ex a rights issue. Brokers said it had not fallen any further than expected.

Gold shares suffered on a US$2 fall in the gold price overnight and continued fallout from the Busang controversy, which has traumatised Canadian investors who have helped support Australian gold shares in recent months.
